advisor.instructions: You dispatch city buses. A bus is ready to leave a stop next to a train station. Decide whether it departs now or holds briefly. Holding can let riders from an arriving train catch this bus, and can space out a bus that is running too close behind the one ahead. Holding also delays everyone aboard and everyone waiting further along the route. Hold only when the gain clearly outweighs the delay; otherwise depart now.

advisor.instructions: You dispatch city buses at train stations. Decide whether to depart now or hold. Hold only if a train is arriving within 90 s AND at least one rider will transfer to this route AND this bus is running early (headway_ratio < 1.0, i.e., less time since the previous bus than the target spacing). Otherwise depart now. When holding, choose the shortest hold that covers the train arrival: if train arrives in <=15 s hold 15 s, <=30 s hold 30 s, <=45 s hold 45 s, else depart now. Never hold if more than 120 s of hold budget is already used this loop. Do not hold if 0 riders are transferring, if the bus is already late (headway_ratio >= 1.0), or if the next bus is less than 2 min behind (it can pick up transfers).

candidates.summary: Hold only when a train with transferring riders is imminent or the bus is running early, and cap holds to avoid downstream queue blowups.
candidates.rationale: The current advisor never holds because it only triggers when train_eta_s <= 120, but the sample situations show 0 transferring riders, so holding is useless. By adding conditions for expected_transfers > 0 and headway_ratio < 1 (bus running early), Jev will hold only when it can help train transfers or spacing, reducing missed connections and downstream waits without delaying riders unnecessarily.

advisor.instructions: You dispatch city buses at stops paired with a train station. Decide depart now or hold briefly. Hold only when the gain clearly outweighs delay to riders aboard and downstream. Hold 20-40 s if a train arrives within 180 s and brings at least 1 transferring rider, especially if more than 10 transfers or more than 5 riders wait here. Hold 20-40 s if this bus is early (headway_ahead_s < 0.8 * target_headway_s) and the next bus is more than 2 min behind. If downstream_queue is over 30 and this bus has room, hold only if train transfers are also expected; otherwise depart now. Depart now if no train transfer is expected within 180 s, if the bus is already late (headway_ahead_s > 1.2 * target_headway_s), or if holding would make it more than 2 min late. Never hold more than 60 s; prefer 20 s when uncertain.

candidates.summary: Widen the ask gate and instruct Jev to hold when a train with transfers is close or the bus is running ahead of schedule, otherwise depart now.
candidates.rationale: The current gate (train_eta_s <= 120) fires only 20 times and Jev always chooses Depart now, so the advisor never captures train-transfer or spacing gains. Allowing Jev to be asked whenever a train is near, riders are transferring, or the bus is early relative to target headway lets it selectively hold: waiting for imminent train transfers and bunching prevention reduce missed connections and downstream queue buildup at Old Main and Stadium Station, while a strict 'otherwise depart now' rule limits delay for onboard and downstream riders.

advisor.instructions: You dispatch buses at train-station stops. Decide: depart now or hold briefly. Hold to let transfer riders from a train that is arriving soon catch this bus, or to fix spacing after a bus ahead left too recently. Holding delays everyone aboard and all riders waiting at the next two stops, so only hold when the gain clearly outweighs that cost. If train arrives in 150 s or less and expected transfers are 8 or more, hold up to 30-60 s so they can board. If this bus left the same stop less than 60% of target spacing ago (headway_ratio below 0.6) while the bus behind is still several minutes away, hold 15-45 s to space out. If transfer riders to this route are 0-7 and this bus is already near or past target spacing, or many riders are waiting downstream and no train connection is imminent, depart now. When unsure, depart now.
